title: Copper Basin — Channel & Compatibility Framing
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Copper Basin to evaluate channel/reseller fit and technical compatibility for hybrid GPU onramp. Key topics: deployment modes (VPC, dedicated), integration surface for marketplace/reseller, security/compliance (SOC2/SAML/KMS), routing and failover, initial perf/compatibility tests. Agreed next steps include a Redwood SE lab run with Copper Basin sample workloads, sharing partner integration guide and a follow-up deep-dive scheduled for May 6.
next_steps: Liam to run sample perf test against Copper Basin GPU instances (dataset + script provided by Copper Basin)
Maya to share partner integration guide and reseller contract draft
Schedule technical deep dive for 2026-05-06 10:00 PT
Copper Basin to provide 2-week production-like sample workload and traffic profile
action_items: Liam Ortiz: run compatibility perf on m60-class copper nodes with sample dataset (due 2026-05-03)
Maya Chen: send partner integration guide, marketplace onboarding checklist, and pricing rubric (due 2026-04-28)
Evelyn Park: share traffic histogram and sample inference payloads (due 2026-04-30)
Priya Singh: list compliance requirements and encryption/KMS constraints (due 2026-05-04)
transcript:
Header: 2026-04-26 08:00 PT | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Evelyn (Copper Basin Head of Platform), Jonas (Lead SRE), Priya (Security), Samir (Partnerships)
Recorded at (zoom): 2026-04-26T15:00:00Z
Links shared: 'Partner Integration Guide (redwood://partners/guide-v2)', 'copper-basin-specs.xlsx'

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um, quick intros. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood partnerships team. Liam our solutions eng will lead the tech bits.
00:12 Evelyn: hi yeah thanks, evelyn here — we're looking at options to expand our reseller channel and curious about how Redwood would fit as a managed inference onramp to our customers.
00:22 Maya: perfect. high-level first — Redwood supports hosted, dedicated and private deployments. for channel/reseller we usually see two paths: marketplace listing where you resell hosted API, or a dedicated onramp integration where you route customer traffic into copper-basin GPU pools and we provide the runtime + billing hooks.
00:40 Samir: so for the dedicated route, does that mean copper-basin provides the infra and Redwood provides the serving runtime? how much coupling?
00:48 Liam: yeah that's right, typically you host GPU pools — the runtime is lightweight and sits in your VPC if you want private deployments. we can also do hybrid where control plane is Redwood-managed but the inference nodes are in your cloud. there are config knobs — batching, kv-cache, quantization profiles.
01:05 Jonas: when you say 'kv-cache' i'm assuming that's the k-v cache for autoregressive contexts — any special memory footprint we should know about for large seq lengths?
01:13 Liam: good question — for long-seq we do dynamic KV eviction and sharding across GPUs. there will be memory overhead per token, so for 64k-ish sequences we recommend specific instance sizes; we'll share a sizing guide. sometimes the transcriber here writes K-V cash, haha.
01:28 Priya: from security side: we need SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integration. also audit logs with retention controls and the option for on-prem private deployments for EU data residency. how mature are those integrations?
01:44 Maya: we have SOC2 attestation, SAML/SSO and RBAC are supported; KMS integrations exist for both hosted and private. audit logs and retention policies are configurable on the console; for private on-prem we can integrate with customer-managed HSMs. we'll send the security checklist.
02:00 Priya: any gotchas around tokenization or payloads that might leak PII into logs for hosted mode?
02:07 Liam: logs can be redacted and we have options to disable full payload retention for hosted. for stricter customers we do private deployments so no customer data leaves the VPC. sometimes words get munged in the transcript - "payloads" -> "pay loads" — ignore that.
02:23 Evelyn: cool. another concern — latency vs cost. our customers care about 99th percentile latency and also want to minimize cost per token. how do you approach that?
02:33 Liam: we expose batching and auto-batching configs, prefix caching, and quantization profiles. for example, quantized 4-bit models cutting cost by ~2x but might impact some quality-sensitive tasks. we recommend per-workload evals — Redwood Optimize gives tradeoff suggestions.
02:48 Jonas: do you support model variants/fallbacks? e.g., route to cheaper model when capacity is low?
02:55 Maya: yes, smart routing by policy — latency-first, cost-first, region-based. we can configure automatic fallback to smaller variants with A/B rollouts or canary.
03:06 Samir: for the channel model — what's the billing flow? do you invoice through us or via Redwood?
03:12 Maya: flexible. we can do reseller billing where usage is attributed to your account and you resell, or direct marketplace where customers bill through Redwood and you get a revenue share. we'll include the pricing rubric in the doc.
03:25 Evelyn: technical integration — what's the surface area? APIs, SDKs, or a webhook?
03:30 Liam: REST + SDKs (python/node/go), streaming, and a small control API for routing and model pinning. we also provide a gRPC adapter if you prefer. onboarding typically includes a small agent for metrics/export and optional gateway for VPC tunneling.
03:46 Jonas: any prebuilt terraform modules or helm charts for spinning up the runtime in our clusters?
03:52 Liam: yes, we have helm charts and terraform modules; we also provide a quickstart repo with a sample helm values file for Azure/GCP/AWS. we'll share that repo link.
04:05 Priya: about compliance again — do you support customer-managed keys only in private mode, or can hosted also use customer KMS?
04:13 Maya: hosted can integrate with customer KMS through a dedicated connection in many cases but for the strictest customers we recommend private deployment. it's an engineering tradeoff.
04:24 Jonas: performance testing — we'd want a bench with our sample models and dataset. can Redwood run an initial run to help us scope required GPU count?
04:33 Liam: yes, we can run a perf lab. if you share a small workload and traffic profile we'll run tests against our internal infra and also a mirrored run on cu-basin nodes if you want.
04:45 Evelyn: that'd be ideal. target timeline would be pilot in June.
04:50 Maya: sounds reasonable. pilot scope: 3 customer tenants, baseline model variant, SLA targets (p99 < 300ms for small prompts). is that aligned?
05:02 Jonas: p99 < 300ms for short prompts is a good target. for long conversational workloads p99 will naturally be higher.
05:10 Priya: one more: auditability — we need immutable logs with export to SIEM. is that straightforward?
05:16 Liam: yes, logs export to S3/Blob or SIEM via export connectors; we support log immutability and signed audit trails.
05:25 Samir: okay commercial question — margins, partner discount tiers, and co-marketing?
05:30 Maya: we have partner tiers based on committed volume; first pilot gets preferred onboarding support. co-marketing is possible after initial success metrics. I'll include the partner program doc.
05:42 Evelyn: awesome. any blockers for us to start the perf run? we can share datasets and a sandbox account.
05:48 Liam: best is to share sample payloads and a traffic trace (CSV) and grant a sandbox API key. we'll need SSH access if you want us to run against your GPU nodes.
05:59 Evelyn: we'll prepare that.
06:03 Maya: cool — recap: Maya to share partner integration guide, partner program and pricing rubric; Liam to run perf with data Copper Basin provides; schedule deep dive 2026-05-06; copper basin to send sample workload and traffic profile.
06:18 Jonas: thanks, that's clear. one note — we've seen some doc transcriptions where model names get garbled (eg 'redwood dedicated' -> 'redwood dedicateded'), so we'll rely on the deck you share.
06:30 Priya: I'll consolidate security reqs and share.
06:34 Maya: perfect. thanks all. we'll follow up in email with calendar invite for May 6 and links.
06:40 End.
